facts.label: Quarterly reports for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026
facts.text: All three are unaudited condensed consolidated statements of Block, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries. Period labels are confirmed in the text: "For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2026" (Q3 report, page:1), "For the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026" and "For the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026". The Q3 report carries the balance sheet at September 30, 2026 against December 31, 2025 (pages 4 to 5), the statements of operations for three and nine months (page:5), cash flows (pages 8 to 9), and Note 12 on indebtedness (pages 26 to 29). The Q1 and Q2 reports hold Note 12 at page:23 and page:25 respectively, which supports quarter-by-quarter debt movements. The Q3 report states the perimeter: "Block is comprised of two reportable segments, Square and Cash App." (page:9), with a corporate and other category in Note 17 (pages 38 to 39). The reports consolidate the Warehouse special purpose entities, which are separate legal entities whose assets "are not available to satisfy the claims of the Company or those of its creditors" (page:29); this is an entity-perimeter distinction that downstream work must preserve.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Block, Inc. reports a platform business with two reportable segments and a revenue base that grew in 2026 on payments volume and consumer lending. Its debt at September 30, 2026 consists of five note series (four senior unsecured series and one convertible series) with 5,775.0 of principal, secured warehouse borrowings of 1,543.5 held in special purpose entities whose assets are not available to the issuer's creditors, and an undrawn 900.0 revolver. Cash and cash equivalents of 7,859.3 exceed total debt of 7,318.5, so net debt is negative on that measure. On the filed basis (operating income plus depreciation and amortization, no add-backs) LTM EBITDA is 1,567.0, giving total debt to EBITDA of 4.67x, up from 4.19x at FY2025, and EBITDA to cash interest of 3.99x, down from 8.44x. On management's Adjusted EBITDA of 4,336.4 the same ratios are 1.69x and 11.03x. The gap between the two bases is mostly share-based compensation (about 1.2 billion a year) and "contingencies, restructuring and other charges", which were 1,542.9 for nine months 2026 (742.8 + 365.1 + 435.0). Separately, accrued legal contingencies on the balance sheet rose to 980.6 at the latest quarter from 173.0 at FY2025, and include 764 for a Department of Justice resolution agreed in principle in October 2026 and accrued at September 30, 2026. That payment is a cash claim outside the debt figure. The reported cash flow is flattered by the unpaid accrual. The view is therefore moderate gross leverage with ample stated liquidity, a bond maturity profile with nothing due until November 2027, and meaningful non-debt claims and definition risk that the covenant (a maximum total net leverage ratio, level not printed) cannot be tested against from the pack.

facts.label: Quality and definition review
facts.text: Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income excluding share-based compensation, restructuring share-based compensation, depreciation and amortization, "contingencies, restructuring, and other charges", interest, bitcoin remeasurement, other income and expense, taxes, disposals and acquired deferred revenue adjustments (letter page:22). Quarterly add-backs for contingencies, restructuring and other charges were 54.1 (Q4 2025), 742.8 (Q1 2026), 365.1 (Q2 2026) and 435.0 (Q3 2026) (letter page:32). The filings tie the increase in general and administrative expense to accrued legal contingencies (letter page:16) and the Workforce Plan cost 495.0 in nine months 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:40); the pages read do not itemise how much of the add-back is the Department of Justice matter, for which "The Company has accrued $764 million for this matter as of September 30, 2026" (10-Q Q3 page:34). Because the accrual is unpaid, nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of 3,001.6 includes a positive swing from accrued legal contingencies (10-Q Q3 page:59: "primarily due to an increase in accrued legal contingencies"); accrued legal contingencies rose by 807.6. The financial covenant is "a maximum total net leverage ratio" tested quarterly (10-Q Q3 page:28), with the issuer stating compliance; its definition, addbacks and threshold are not printed, so neither basis above is the covenant measure.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Block, Inc. is an operating company with two reportable segments, Square for sellers and Cash App for consumers, and a third revenue lens of commerce enablement, financial solutions and bitcoin ecosystem. It has no sponsor, no leveraged transaction and no acquisition financing in the sources. The transaction history that matters to creditors is a series of unsecured note issues (the 2032 notes in 2024, the 2030 and 2033 notes on August 18, 2025), the repayment in cash of two 2026 maturities, the January 14, 2026 amendment that enlarged the revolver and replaced its financial covenant with a maximum total net leverage ratio, a larger share repurchase authorization, and, after the quarter end but before the filing, agreements in principle on a Department of Justice deferred prosecution matter and a derivative-suit settlement. Control rests with Class B holders with ten votes per share, and the founder is described as controlling shareholder in the bank-regulatory commitments for Square Financial Services. Documented issuer behaviour is Neutral or Mixed: debt was repaid from cash and the revolver enlarged, but repurchases continue and 2025 issuance occurred in a year of large repurchases. No priming, uptiering, drop-down, non-pro-rata exchange or collateral release appears in the pages read. The creditor mechanisms to watch are lending growth funded by secured warehouse lines (which sit ahead of note holders on those receivables), the unpaid legal settlements, and the absence of the executed documents that would show restricted payments capacity.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New debt issues. In the nine months of 2026 the company issued no senior notes: the cash flow statement shows no proceeds from issuance of senior notes for 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:8). The last note issue was on August 18, 2025, when 2.2 billion of senior unsecured notes were issued, comprising 1.2 billion of 2030 Senior Notes at 5.625% and 1.0 billion of 2033 Senior Notes at 6.000% (10-K page:188). The 2032 Senior Notes, 2.0 billion at 6.50%, were issued on May 9, 2024 (10-K page:190). In 2025 the company recorded 2.3 billion of share repurchases alongside the 2.2 billion of cash received from that issuance (10-K page:111); the filing does not say the proceeds funded the repurchases, so the link is an Analyst Interpretation of timing only.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Repayments and facility changes. The 2026 Convertible Notes (575.0) were paid in cash at maturity on May 1, 2026 and the 2026 Senior Notes (1,000.0) on June 1, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:27), leaving note principal of 5,775.0 across the 2027 Convertible Notes and the 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033 Senior Notes. On January 14, 2026 the revolving credit agreement was amended and restated, raising commitments from 775 to 900, extending maturity to January 14, 2031 with a springing earlier date if liquidity would fall below 250 after repaying existing notes at maturity, and replacing the prior financial covenant with a maximum total net leverage ratio tested quarterly; the revolver is undrawn (10-Q Q3 page:28). Warehouse borrowings stood at 1,543.5, with a total of 2.4 billion of capacity and 809.3 available, and final maturities through July 2029 (10-Q Q3 page:29). Brokered certificates of deposit of 381.4 par began in Q3 2026 at a weighted average rate of 4.09% (10-Q Q3 page:56).

Warehouse borrowings stood at 1,543.5, with a total of 2.4 billion of capacity and 809.3 available, and final maturities through July 2029 (10-Q Q3 page:29). Brokered certificates of deposit of 381.4 par began in Q3 2026 at a weighted average rate of 4.09% (10-Q Q3 page:56).

facts.text: Subsequent events and pending items (after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet date, before the November 3, 2026 filing and the cutoff). The filing says losses in excess of the accrual are reasonably possible (10-Q Q3 page:35). Also in October 2026 the parties to the shareholder derivative actions agreed in principle to a global resolution including a 150 million payment from the defendants' insurers to the company, subject to court approval (10-Q Q3 page:36). The securities class action remains pending after the motion to dismiss was denied on January 6, 2026, with an accrual that the filing calls not material and a possible loss in excess that could be material (10-Q Q3 page:35). These items are subsequent events or pending matters and are not folded into period facts.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: bitcoin ecosystem was 27% of Q3 2026 revenue and 2% of gross profit, while commerce enablement and financial solutions revenue grew 16% and 31% in the quarter (10-Q Q3 page:44). Mechanic: revenue volatility from bitcoin prices does not transmit to gross profit, which depends on payments volume and lending. Implication: debt service capacity rests on payments and lending gross profit, so monitoring should use gross profit and loss rates, not headline revenue. Counter: no logged conflict. 2. Funding structure. Evidence: warehouse borrowings of 1,543.5 secured on receivables held in special purpose entities, and 381.4 of brokered certificates of deposit (10-Q Q3 pages 29, 56). Mechanic: lending growth is financed ahead of unsecured note holders on those assets and by deposit funding conditional on the bank staying well capitalized. Implication: recovery prospects for unsecured notes on the lending assets are weaker than headline asset totals suggest; no recovery conclusion is drawn here. Counter: no logged conflict. 3. Legal claims. Evidence: an accrual of 764 million for the Department of Justice resolution and the statement that losses in excess are reasonably possible (10-Q Q3 pages 34, 35). Mechanic: an unpaid, non-debt cash claim reduces liquidity when settled and is excluded from debt leverage ratios. Implication: net leverage and liquidity on the filed basis overstate headroom until the payment is made; monitor court approval and payment timing. Counter: the 150 million insurer receipt, if approved, is a partial offset, not logged as a conflict. 4. Capital allocation. Evidence: 2025 issuance of 2.2 billion beside 2.3 billion of repurchases, and 2026 repayment of 1,575.0 from cash alongside 700.9 of repurchases. Mechanic: shareholder returns compete with deleveraging for the same cash. Implication: leverage tolerance appears to be managed with cash buffers; no leverage target was located in the pages read, and the covenant level is not printed. Counter: no logged conflict.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Block, Inc. has a moderate credit profile: strong stated liquidity is set against leverage that looks high on filed earnings and low on management's adjusted earnings. The strongest support is liquidity: USD 7,859.3 million of cash and cash equivalents and an undrawn USD 900.0 million revolver, against USD 5,775.0 million of note principal and no note due before the 2027 convertible. The weakest point is earnings quality: total debt to EBITDA is 4.67x on the filed basis but 1.69x on management's Adjusted EBITDA, because share-based compensation and large legal charges are added back, while USD 764 million for the Department of Justice matter is accrued but unpaid. The outcome turns on the final size and timing of the legal payments, the unpublished covenant level and whether credit losses in the growing lending book stay contained.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, Block's liquidity is its main credit support: cash and cash equivalents of USD 7,859.3 million and an undrawn USD 900.0 million revolver exceed total debt of USD 7,318.5 million, and no note matures before the USD 575.0 million convertible in November 2027, so near-term refinancing exposure is mostly in the secured warehouse lines, whose final maturities are USD 515.0 million in 2027 (USD 447.4 million of it classified current), rather than the bond stack. Second, leverage is highly sensitive to the earnings definition: filed-basis total debt to EBITDA rose from 4.19x at FY2025 to 4.67x at LTM Q3 2026 while interest cover fell from 8.44x to 3.99x, whereas management's basis shows 1.69x and 11.03x; the add-backs include contingencies, restructuring and other charges and share-based compensation, so the covenant outcome cannot be inferred. Third, legal claims sit outside the debt figures: USD 764 million is accrued for the Department of Justice matter, accrued legal contingencies rose from USD 173.0 million to USD 980.6 million, and the filing says losses above the accrual are reasonably possible; a USD 150 million insurer payment in the derivative settlement is a possible partial offset but is not final. Fourth, reported operating cash flow less capital expenditure of USD 3,453.4 million over the LTM period is flattered by this unpaid accrual and excludes lending outflows. Fifth, lending growth increases funding reliance on secured warehouse borrowings of USD 1,543.5 million and brokered certificates of deposit of USD 381.4 million, which rank ahead of unsecured note holders on those assets and depend on the bank subsidiary remaining well capitalized.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. (1) Liquidity and maturity profile, Documentary Fact: stated liquidity of USD 10,064.0 million, the undrawn revolver maturing in January 2031, note maturities spread from 2027 to 2033 and the 2026 maturities of USD 1,575.0 million repaid in cash, which supports debt service without market access (an Analyst Interpretation). (2) Gross profit mix, Documentary Fact: payments and lending drive gross profit while bitcoin revenue, 27% of Q3 2026 revenue, contributes 2% of gross profit, so bitcoin price swings change revenue more than earnings. (3) Fixed-rate unsecured note stack, Analyst Interpretation: coupons from 0.25% to 6.50% give a run-rate annual coupon of USD 293.9 million on USD 5,775.0 million of principal, about 18.8% of the add-back-free LTM EBITDA of USD 1,567.0 million (a calculated share), so the fixed charge looks manageable if earnings hold.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. (1) Add-back dependence, Documentary Fact for the figures and Analyst Interpretation for the reading: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 4,336.4 million is more than double filed EBITDA of USD 1,567.0 million, and contingencies charges recur across 2026 quarters, so the add-backs are not one-off in the period. (2) Unpaid legal claims, Documentary Fact: the accrual and the possibility of excess losses are claims outside debt that will draw on cash, and the final agreement and court approval are pending. (3) Credit losses in a growing lending book, Documentary Fact: transaction, loan and consumer receivable losses were USD 601.7 million in Q3 2026 against USD 363.5 million a year earlier, which reduces operating income directly. (4) Customer cash, Analyst Interpretation: customers payable exceed customer funds by USD 2,343.2 million before USD 1,454.2 million of settlements receivable, a residual of USD 889.0 million that corporate cash may fund, so net debt of negative USD 540.8 million may overstate surplus cash. (5) Control and capital allocation, Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation: Class B holders control a majority of votes, and share repurchases of USD 700.9 million in 2026 compete with deleveraging for the same cash.

Cash plus revolver minus total debt: 7,859.3 + 900.0 = 8,759.3; total debt 7,318.5; cash alone exceeds total debt by 7,859.3 - 7,318.5 = 540.8 (equal to the negative net debt of 540.8). 2. ### Readiness view

Overall view: READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for the four selected downstream consumers. The effective source set is the annual report for FY2025, the three 2026 quarterly reports and the three 2026 shareholder letters. Each of the four filed reports carries a balance sheet, a statement of operations, cash flows and an indebtedness note, so the evidence a debt, liquidity and operating-trend analysis needs is located and retained. The strongest contrary evidence is that none of the executed legal documents are in the pack and the financial covenant level is not printed, so the legal terms of the debt rest on the issuer's own summaries in the notes. The Q3 2026 report is the latest filed document and controls any conflict with the shareholder letters. Nothing in the pack is dated after the cutoff; the latest filing is dated 2026-11-03.
### Source-by-source assessment
#### Annual report for FY2025

Audited annual report for Block, Inc. as the registrant. The cover reads "For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025" (page:1). The auditor's reports are retained: "We have served as the Company’s auditor since 2019." (page:139). The indebtedness note is Note 14 (page:184) and the 2025 year-end note list includes the 2026 Senior Notes and 2026 Convertible Notes that were later repaid. Coupon terms are printed there, for example "bear interest at a rate of 6.50% payable semi-annually on May 15 and November 15 of each year" for the 2032 Senior Notes (page:190). The exhibit list names the indentures: "4.7 Indenture, dated as of May 20, 2021, by and between Square, Inc. and Bank of New York Mel" (page:215), which shows the notes were issued under the former corporate name; the indentures are incorporated by reference and not supplied. Extraction status is complete (219 of 219 pages), but a successful extraction is not a fidelity review.
#### Quarterly reports for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026

All three are unaudited condensed consolidated statements of Block, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries. Period labels are confirmed in the text: "For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2026" (Q3 report, page:1), "For the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026" and "For the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026". The Q3 report carries the balance sheet at September 30, 2026 against December 31, 2025 (pages 4 to 5), the statements of operations for three and nine months (page:5), cash flows (pages 8 to 9), and Note 12 on indebtedness (pages 26 to 29). ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Block's notes and secured warehouse borrowings sit below its reported cash, with leverage on filed earnings of 4.67x at the latest quarter and 1.69x on management's adjusted earnings. Large unpaid legal accruals weaken the picture. | Medium | The covenant level is not printed, and adjusted earnings add back large legal charges and share-based pay. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Debt at the latest quarter is the notes plus warehouse borrowings, and the 2026 notes were paid in cash. | No bond maturity falls before 2027, and near-term refinancing risk is limited to the warehouse lines and short certificates of deposit. | High |

| Leverage on filed operating income plus depreciation rose from 4.19x at FY2025 to 4.67x at the latest quarter, while net of cash it moved from 1.04x to below zero. | Net leverage depends on cash that may partly fund customer balances, so the negative net figure may overstate surplus cash. | Medium |

| Operating income fell on large legal and restructuring charges, and an agreed Department of Justice resolution is accrued but not yet paid. | Cash outflows for the settlement are still ahead, so reported operating cash flow overstates what is free. | Medium |
| Interest cover on filed earnings fell from 8.44x to 3.99x. | The decline reflects higher cash interest and lower filed earnings over the latest twelve months. | Medium |

| Stated liquidity of 10,064.0 includes restricted cash and securities, and the revolver is undrawn. | Liquidity is large against near-term maturities, but not all of it is freely available corporate cash. | Medium |
### Financial base view

Block, Inc. reports a platform business with two reportable segments and a revenue base that grew in 2026 on payments volume and consumer lending. Its debt at September 30, 2026 consists of five note series (four senior unsecured series and one convertible series) with 5,775.0 of principal, secured warehouse borrowings of 1,543.5 held in special purpose entities whose assets are not available to the issuer's creditors, and an undrawn 900.0 revolver. Cash and cash equivalents of 7,859.3 exceed total debt of 7,318.5, so net debt is negative on that measure. On the filed basis (operating income plus depreciation and amortization, no add-backs) LTM EBITDA is 1,567.0, giving total debt to EBITDA of 4.67x, up from 4.19x at FY2025, and EBITDA to cash interest of 3.99x, down from 8.44x. On management's Adjusted EBITDA of 4,336.4 the same ratios are 1.69x and 11.03x. The gap between the two bases is mostly share-based compensation (about 1.2 billion a year) and "contingencies, restructuring and other charges", which were 1,542.9 for nine months 2026 (742.8 + 365.1 + 435.0). Separately, accrued legal contingencies on the balance sheet rose to 980.6 at the latest quarter from 173.0 at FY2025, and include 764 for a Department of Justice resolution agreed in principle in October 2026 and accrued at September 30, 2026. That payment is a cash claim outside the debt figure. The reported cash flow is flattered by the unpaid accrual. The view is therefore moderate gross leverage with ample stated liquidity, a bond maturity profile with nothing due until November 2027, and meaningful non-debt claims and definition risk that the covenant (a maximum total net leverage ratio, level not printed) cannot be tested against from the pack.

### Quality and definition review

Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income excluding share-based compensation, restructuring share-based compensation, depreciation and amortization, "contingencies, restructuring, and other charges", interest, bitcoin remeasurement, other income and expense, taxes, disposals and acquired deferred revenue adjustments (letter page:22). Quarterly add-backs for contingencies, restructuring and other charges were 54.1 (Q4 2025), 742.8 (Q1 2026), 365.1 (Q2 2026) and 435.0 (Q3 2026) (letter page:32). The filings tie the increase in general and administrative expense to accrued legal contingencies (letter page:16) and the Workforce Plan cost 495.0 in nine months 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:40); the pages read do not itemise how much of the add-back is the Department of Justice matter, for which "The Company has accrued $764 million for this matter as of September 30, 2026" (10-Q Q3 page:34). Because the accrual is unpaid, nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of 3,001.6 includes a positive swing from accrued legal contingencies (10-Q Q3 page:59: "primarily due to an increase in accrued legal contingencies"); accrued legal contingencies rose by 807.6. The financial covenant is "a maximum total net leverage ratio" tested quarterly (10-Q Q3 page:28), with the issuer stating compliance; its definition, addbacks and threshold are not printed, so neither basis above is the covenant measure.

Lending flows affect comparability: loans held for investment are classified in investing activities (purchases and originations 33,272.9 and repayments 31,325.9 for nine months 2026, 10-Q Q3 page:8), while loans originally held for sale run through operating activities. Operating cash flow less capex therefore does not net lending growth, and the company's own non-GAAP cash flow after those items is 1,697 LTM (letter page:17), a management figure.

All inputs in US$m from the cited pages; thousands converted by dividing by 1,000.

3. Total debt (note principal plus Warehouse Facilities drawn). FY2025: 7,350.000 + (466.942 + 897.941) = 8,714.883. Q3 2026: 5,775.000 + (447.437 + 1,096.103) = 7,318.540. Warehouse total agrees to the scheduled principal table: 515.039 + 549.437 + 479.064 = 1,543.540.

7. Run-rate coupon on notes at September 30, 2026 = 1,200 x 5.625% + 1,000 x 3.50% + 2,000 x 6.50% + 1,000 x 6.000% + 575 x 0.25% = 67.5 + 35.0 + 130.0 + 60.0 + 1.4375 = 293.9375. This is a calculated annual contractual coupon, not a filed figure; nine months 2026 contractual interest on the notes was 231.370 (10-Q Q3 page:27), consistent with this rate plus five months on the repaid 2.75% 2026 Senior Notes (1,000 x 2.75% x 5/12 = 11.46; 293.94 x 9/12 = 220.45; sum 231.9).

8. Customers payable versus customer funds at September 30, 2026: 7,700.091 - 5,356.911 = 2,343.180 excess of customers payable over customer funds; less settlements receivable 1,454.211 leaves 888.969. This is an analytical indicator that some corporate cash may fund customer obligations; the filing does not state the amount (10-Q Q3 page:59 explains customers payable can exceed settlements receivable and includes Cash App stored funds).
9. Change in accrued legal contingencies: 980.592 - 172.959 = 807.633.

Not calculable. | Covenant headroom cannot be computed; both EBITDA bases above differ from the covenant definition. |

| Guarantors and obligor roles | Not stated in the pages read; context blank. | Structural subordination relative to subsidiaries and the Warehouse SPEs is not assessable beyond the SPE description. |

| Quarterly cash interest | Cash paid for interest is printed for FY2025 and nine months 2025 and 2026 only; Q3 2025 and Q3 2026 discrete cash interest is not supplied. | Interest cover is shown for FY2025 and LTM only. |

| Rounded quarterly operating cash flow and capex | Q3 2025 and Q3 2026 operating cash flow and capex come from the shareholder letter in US$m rounded; not recomputed from filed three-month statements because the 10-Q cash flow is nine-month only. | Marked rounded in the table. |
| Customer cash | The share of cash and cash equivalents that is economically owed to customers is not stated. | Net debt of -540.8 may overstate surplus cash. |

| DOJ resolution | Agreement in principle, subject to final agreement and court approval; the filing says terms could exceed the amount accrued (10-Q Q3 pages 34 and 35). The cash timing is not stated. | Cash outflow of about 764 net is not in debt or in the leverage ratios; the derivative-case insurance receipt of 150 is also uncertain (page:36). |

| Other non-debt claims | Purchase commitments total 2,201.3 (10-Q Q3 page:37); operating leases, pensions and retiree medical, factoring and supply-chain finance were not examined in this module beyond that; interest-bearing deposits and brokered certificates of deposit of 381.4 are bank-funding liabilities outside the debt figure. | Left for CP-2. |
| Ratings | The context supplies none; the 10-Q mentions agency ratings in management discussion (page:58) only as issuer statements. | Not verified against agency reports. |

| Perimeter | Figures are consolidated Block, Inc. including Square Financial Services and the Warehouse SPEs; the filings do not give restricted and unrestricted subsidiary splits. | Whole-group metrics, not issuer-only. |
## Next module

CP-1A should reuse the LTM bridge above (quarter sums agree to FY2025 less nine months 2025 plus nine months 2026) and test the Adjusted EBITDA add-backs, especially contingencies, restructuring and other charges and share-based compensation, as the main definition risk. CP-2 should take the maturity table, the note coupons, the Warehouse Facilities terms and the non-debt claims listed in the gaps (DOJ accrual of 764, accrued legal contingencies of 980.6, purchase commitments of 2,201.3, brokered certificates of deposit of 381.4), and request the indentures and credit agreement if covenant analysis is required. Carry forward that the leverage ratios above are on a filed-earnings basis with no covenant adjustments.

### Business and transaction view

It has no sponsor, no leveraged transaction and no acquisition financing in the sources. The transaction history that matters to creditors is a series of unsecured note issues (the 2032 notes in 2024, the 2030 and 2033 notes on August 18, 2025), the repayment in cash of two 2026 maturities, the January 14, 2026 amendment that enlarged the revolver and replaced its financial covenant with a maximum total net leverage ratio, a larger share repurchase authorization, and, after the quarter end but before the filing, agreements in principle on a Department of Justice deferred prosecution matter and a derivative-suit settlement. Control rests with Class B holders with ten votes per share, and the founder is described as controlling shareholder in the bank-regulatory commitments for Square Financial Services. Documented issuer behaviour is Neutral or Mixed: debt was repaid from cash and the revolver enlarged, but repurchases continue and 2025 issuance occurred in a year of large repurchases. No priming, uptiering, drop-down, non-pro-rata exchange or collateral release appears in the pages read. The creditor mechanisms to watch are lending growth funded by secured warehouse lines (which sit ahead of note holders on those receivables), the unpaid legal settlements, and the absence of the executed documents that would show restricted payments capacity.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

There is no transaction document, sponsor, use-of-proceeds statement or acquisition financing for 2026 in the sources, so no transaction row is built beyond the financing history below; that absence is Insufficient Information, not an adverse conclusion.

New debt issues. In the nine months of 2026 the company issued no senior notes: the cash flow statement shows no proceeds from issuance of senior notes for 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:8). The last note issue was on August 18, 2025, when 2.2 billion of senior unsecured notes were issued, comprising 1.2 billion of 2030 Senior Notes at 5.625% and 1.0 billion of 2033 Senior Notes at 6.000% (10-K page:188). The 2032 Senior Notes, 2.0 billion at 6.50%, were issued on May 9, 2024 (10-K page:190). In 2025 the company recorded 2.3 billion of share repurchases alongside the 2.2 billion of cash received from that issuance (10-K page:111); the filing does not say the proceeds funded the repurchases, so the link is an Analyst Interpretation of timing only.

Repayments and facility changes. The 2026 Convertible Notes (575.0) were paid in cash at maturity on May 1, 2026 and the 2026 Senior Notes (1,000.0) on June 1, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:27), leaving note principal of 5,775.0 across the 2027 Convertible Notes and the 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033 Senior Notes. On January 14, 2026 the revolving credit agreement was amended and restated, raising commitments from 775 to 900, extending maturity to January 14, 2031 with a springing earlier date if liquidity would fall below 250 after repaying existing notes at maturity, and replacing the prior financial covenant with a maximum total net leverage ratio tested quarterly; the revolver is undrawn (10-Q Q3 page:28). Warehouse borrowings stood at 1,543.5, with a total of 2.4 billion of capacity and 809.3 available, and final maturities through July 2029 (10-Q Q3 page:29). Brokered certificates of deposit of 381.4 par began in Q3 2026 at a weighted average rate of 4.09% (10-Q Q3 page:56).

Subsequent events and pending items (after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet date, before the November 3, 2026 filing and the cutoff). In October 2026 the company and the Department of Justice reached an agreement in principle to resolve the Bank Secrecy Act inquiry by a three-year deferred prosecution agreement, with a gross monetary component of approximately 964 million and a net payment of approximately 764 million after credit for prior regulatory resolutions; 764 million was accrued at September 30, 2026, and the resolution remains subject to a final agreement and court approval (10-Q Q3 page:34). The filing says losses in excess of the accrual are reasonably possible (10-Q Q3 page:35). Also in October 2026 the parties to the shareholder derivative actions agreed in principle to a global resolution including a 150 million payment from the defendants' insurers to the company, subject to court approval (10-Q Q3 page:36). The securities class action remains pending after the motion to dismiss was denied on January 6, 2026, with an accrual that the filing calls not material and a possible loss in excess that could be material (10-Q Q3 page:35). These items are subsequent events or pending matters and are not folded into period facts.

Assessed behaviour category: Neutral or Mixed, with Medium evidence quality (primary dated filings; no executed legal documents).
### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: bitcoin ecosystem was 27% of Q3 2026 revenue and 2% of gross profit, while commerce enablement and financial solutions revenue grew 16% and 31% in the quarter (10-Q Q3 page:44). Mechanic: revenue volatility from bitcoin prices does not transmit to gross profit, which depends on payments volume and lending. Implication: debt service capacity rests on payments and lending gross profit, so monitoring should use gross profit and loss rates, not headline revenue. Counter: no logged conflict.

2. Funding structure. Evidence: warehouse borrowings of 1,543.5 secured on receivables held in special purpose entities, and 381.4 of brokered certificates of deposit (10-Q Q3 pages 29, 56). Mechanic: lending growth is financed ahead of unsecured note holders on those assets and by deposit funding conditional on the bank staying well capitalized. Implication: recovery prospects for unsecured notes on the lending assets are weaker than headline asset totals suggest; no recovery conclusion is drawn here. Counter: no logged conflict.

3. Legal claims. Evidence: an accrual of 764 million for the Department of Justice resolution and the statement that losses in excess are reasonably possible (10-Q Q3 pages 34, 35). Mechanic: an unpaid, non-debt cash claim reduces liquidity when settled and is excluded from debt leverage ratios. Implication: net leverage and liquidity on the filed basis overstate headroom until the payment is made; monitor court approval and payment timing. Counter: the 150 million insurer receipt, if approved, is a partial offset, not logged as a conflict.

4. Capital allocation. Evidence: 2025 issuance of 2.2 billion beside 2.3 billion of repurchases, and 2026 repayment of 1,575.0 from cash alongside 700.9 of repurchases. Mechanic: shareholder returns compete with deleveraging for the same cash. Implication: leverage tolerance appears to be managed with cash buffers; no leverage target was located in the pages read, and the covenant level is not printed. Counter: no logged conflict.

No conflict between sources was found in the facts used. Presentation differences were checked and are not conflicts: the Q3 2026 balance sheet shows other current assets at December 31, 2025 of 4,107.7 (10-Q Q3 page:4), while the FY2025 annual report shows 3,589.9 plus short-term debt securities of 517.8 (10-K page:140), which sum to the same figure (3,589.925 + 517.777 = 4,107.702, in thousands). Shares outstanding at September 30, 2026 (544,541 thousand Class A) and October 30, 2026 (544,546 thousand) differ by dates. The Department of Justice gross (964 million) and net (764 million) amounts are explained in the filing as before and after credit for prior resolutions. The financial handoff's 764 matches.

### Credit view

Block, Inc. has a moderate credit profile: strong stated liquidity is set against leverage that looks high on filed earnings and low on management's adjusted earnings. The strongest support is liquidity: USD 7,859.3 million of cash and cash equivalents and an undrawn USD 900.0 million revolver, against USD 5,775.0 million of note principal and no note due before the 2027 convertible. The weakest point is earnings quality: total debt to EBITDA is 4.67x on the filed basis but 1.69x on management's Adjusted EBITDA, because share-based compensation and large legal charges are added back, while USD 764 million for the Department of Justice matter is accrued but unpaid. The outcome turns on the final size and timing of the legal payments, the unpublished covenant level and whether credit losses in the growing lending book stay contained.
### Credit assessment
| Element | Content | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view | Moderate profile: ample liquidity and no near-term bond maturity, offset by add-back dependent earnings, unpaid legal claims and a growing secured-funded lending book | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | [CP-1] leverage, cover, liquidity and maturity tables; [CP-1A] funding structure and subsequent events |

| Thesis | Block can meet its debt service from liquidity and gross profit in the near term, but the credit depends on legal settlements being paid from cash without damaging liquidity and on lending losses staying controlled | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | same |

| Financial risk, filed basis | Total debt to EBITDA of 4.67x and EBITDA to cash interest of 3.99x at LTM Q3 2026, compared with 4.19x and 8.44x at FY2025 | Documentary Fact | High | [CP-1] chart data |

| Financial risk, adjusted basis | Total debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 1.69x and Adjusted EBITDA to cash interest of 11.03x; management-defined | Management Language | Medium | [CP-1] financial table and definition review |

| Business risk | Two segments, payments volume and consumer lending drive gross profit; bitcoin is 27% of Q3 2026 revenue but 2% of gross profit; dual-class structure in which Class B holders control a majority of votes, with no sponsor | Documentary Fact | High | [CP-1A] company and operating model, company profile |
### Key findings

First, Block's liquidity is its main credit support: cash and cash equivalents of USD 7,859.3 million and an undrawn USD 900.0 million revolver exceed total debt of USD 7,318.5 million, and no note matures before the USD 575.0 million convertible in November 2027, so near-term refinancing exposure is mostly in the secured warehouse lines, whose final maturities are USD 515.0 million in 2027 (USD 447.4 million of it classified current), rather than the bond stack. Second, leverage is highly sensitive to the earnings definition: filed-basis total debt to EBITDA rose from 4.19x at FY2025 to 4.67x at LTM Q3 2026 while interest cover fell from 8.44x to 3.99x, whereas management's basis shows 1.69x and 11.03x; the add-backs include contingencies, restructuring and other charges and share-based compensation, so the covenant outcome cannot be inferred. Third, legal claims sit outside the debt figures: USD 764 million is accrued for the Department of Justice matter, accrued legal contingencies rose from USD 173.0 million to USD 980.6 million, and the filing says losses above the accrual are reasonably possible; a USD 150 million insurer payment in the derivative settlement is a possible partial offset but is not final. Fourth, reported operating cash flow less capital expenditure of USD 3,453.4 million over the LTM period is flattered by this unpaid accrual and excludes lending outflows. Fifth, lending growth increases funding reliance on secured warehouse borrowings of USD 1,543.5 million and brokered certificates of deposit of USD 381.4 million, which rank ahead of unsecured note holders on those assets and depend on the bank subsidiary remaining well capitalized.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. (1) Liquidity and maturity profile, Documentary Fact: stated liquidity of USD 10,064.0 million, the undrawn revolver maturing in January 2031, note maturities spread from 2027 to 2033 and the 2026 maturities of USD 1,575.0 million repaid in cash, which supports debt service without market access (an Analyst Interpretation). (2) Gross profit mix, Documentary Fact: payments and lending drive gross profit while bitcoin revenue, 27% of Q3 2026 revenue, contributes 2% of gross profit, so bitcoin price swings change revenue more than earnings. (3) Fixed-rate unsecured note stack, Analyst Interpretation: coupons from 0.25% to 6.50% give a run-rate annual coupon of USD 293.9 million on USD 5,775.0 million of principal, about 18.8% of the add-back-free LTM EBITDA of USD 1,567.0 million (a calculated share), so the fixed charge looks manageable if earnings hold.

Weaknesses. (1) Add-back dependence, Documentary Fact for the figures and Analyst Interpretation for the reading: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 4,336.4 million is more than double filed EBITDA of USD 1,567.0 million, and contingencies charges recur across 2026 quarters, so the add-backs are not one-off in the period. (2) Unpaid legal claims, Documentary Fact: the accrual and the possibility of excess losses are claims outside debt that will draw on cash, and the final agreement and court approval are pending. (3) Credit losses in a growing lending book, Documentary Fact: transaction, loan and consumer receivable losses were USD 601.7 million in Q3 2026 against USD 363.5 million a year earlier, which reduces operating income directly. (4) Customer cash, Analyst Interpretation: customers payable exceed customer funds by USD 2,343.2 million before USD 1,454.2 million of settlements receivable, a residual of USD 889.0 million that corporate cash may fund, so net debt of negative USD 540.8 million may overstate surplus cash. (5) Control and capital allocation, Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation: Class B holders control a majority of votes, and share repurchases of USD 700.9 million in 2026 compete with deleveraging for the same cash.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Legal payments | Department of Justice resolution (USD 764 million accrued, gross USD 964 million) and further possible losses are paid in cash outside the debt figures | Reduces liquidity and weakens net leverage on settlement; the payment date is unknown | Material |

| Earnings definition and covenant | Maximum total net leverage ratio is tested quarterly under a definition and level that are not printed; filed EBITDA is far below adjusted | Covenant headroom cannot be assessed; a tighter definition than management's would raise leverage towards the filed basis | Material |

| Lending losses and funding | Loss growth in consumer lending reduces operating income, while lending is funded by warehouse lines and deposits that depend on asset performance and bank capital | Stress in receivable performance could reduce warehouse availability (USD 809.3 million) and raise loss pressure at once | Material |
| Customer-fund claims on cash | Customers payable exceed customer funds; part of corporate cash may support customers | Usable liquidity may be lower than stated cash | Minor |

| Structural ranking | Guarantors and indenture terms are not supplied; warehouse assets are not available to the company's creditors | Position of note holders relative to subsidiary creditors cannot be confirmed | Material |
## Calculations
All figures are accepted values from the financial and business handoffs; no new source figure is introduced. Arithmetic done here from those values:
1. Cash plus revolver minus total debt: 7,859.3 + 900.0 = 8,759.3; total debt 7,318.5; cash alone exceeds total debt by 7,859.3 - 7,318.5 = 540.8 (equal to the negative net debt of 540.8).
2. Adjusted EBITDA to filed EBITDA: 4,336.4 / 1,567.0 = 2.77 times, which supports "more than double". Check: 1,567.0 x 2 = 3,134.0, less than 4,336.4.
3. Run-rate coupon share: 293.9 / 1,567.0 = 18.8% of filed LTM EBITDA (a calculated figure, not a filed one; the coupon is the handoff's calculated run-rate).
4. 2027 maturities as stated: 575.0 + 515.0 = 1,090.0 (convertible plus warehouse final maturities; handoff table value 1,090.0).
5. Customer cash residual: 7,700.1 - 5,356.9 = 2,343.2; 2,343.2 - 1,454.2 = 889.0, as in the financial handoff.
6. Repurchase and repayment: 2026 repayments 575.0 + 1,000.0 = 1,575.0 (business handoff).

7. Leverage change: 4.67x - 4.19x = 0.48x increase; cover change 8.44x to 3.99x is a decrease of 4.45x. The periods differ (FY2025 against LTM Q3 2026), so the comparison is across different twelve-month windows.

## Next module

CP-5 should test the evidence base behind this view, in particular the add-back definitions and the legal accruals, and should treat the missing executed documents and covenant level as unresolved. Relative value, security selection and the committee's action bias belong to later modules and are not addressed here.

The strongest evidence against restriction is that every figure traces, the derived figures recompute, and stated liquidity covers the 2027 convertible and warehouse finals many times (cash 7,859.3 against 1,090.0 due in 2027). If the executed credit agreement shows a leverage covenant level far above the filed-basis 4.67x and a definition close to management's adjusted basis, the covenant concern falls away. Downside chain with observable triggers: a final Department of Justice agreement above the 764 accrued (first break: legal accrual) leads to a larger cash payment (transmission), which reduces cash below the 7,859.3 reported and weakens net leverage, then raises covenant sensitivity if the covenant definition does not add back the charges; the trigger is the court-approved final terms and the payment date.
